reviews.text: I went to visit my sister's cat after it had surgery. The nurses were very kind and helpful.

I received excellent care and clear explanations.

Thank you, Dr. Akamatsu.

In June, my dog ​​suddenly became lethargic and developed diarrhea. At first, I thought it was just due to the heat, but he completely stopped eating his favorite food, so I immediately took him to our regular vet.

After examinations, it was discovered that his gums were pale and there was a spinal cord abnormality. We were referred to the Advanced Animal Medical Center Tokyo Hospital, where we went.
With information shared from our regular vet, blood tests and a CT scan were performed.

The result was malignant lymphoma. He's only 5 years old. The situation wasn't good, so he was admitted to the hospital immediately.

He wasn't eating and was severely weakened, so we were prepared for the worst.

After receiving chemotherapy, my child recovered their strength and was discharged after about four days in the hospital. Their recovery was almost miraculous compared to when they were admitted, and we were truly astonished.
A 25-week chemotherapy program was scheduled, aiming for remission, and treatment began.
The progress was good, and the third chemotherapy dose was handed over to our family doctor.
Everything went smoothly until the ninth week, but then lymph node swelling was detected again, and we were transferred back to Tokyo Hospital by our family doctor.
Dr. Takagi, who was in charge, truly cared deeply about my child's condition, considered the best treatment options, and started a new program.
My child became so healthy that we doubted they were even ill, and our whole family was overjoyed.
However, before starting this treatment, we were informed that while the cancer would be suppressed, the risk of infection would increase.
In September, just before the third dose of the new program, their condition worsened again. Tests confirmed that the cancer was suppressed, but an infection was present. We continued treatment hoping for another recovery, but sadly, my beloved child did not recover and passed away.

Thanks to the compassionate treatment I received at Tokyo Hospital, I was able to spend fulfilling and meaningful time in a situation I had once given up on. I am truly grateful to the doctor.

When I informed the doctor of my passing, he grieved as much as a member of the family, and I truly feel fortunate to have been treated by him.

I am grateful for the beautiful flowers and heartfelt message I received from the hospital.

Thank you so much, Dr. Takagi.

My dog ​​has early-stage mitral valve insufficiency, and his liver cysts have more than doubled compared to last year. My regular vet recommended that we first determine if anesthesia is possible, considering his heart condition, and if so, perform a CT scan and treat the cysts. He recommended this hospital, which he trusts the most.

As expected, it was expensive, but they performed a thorough examination, confirmed anesthesia was possible, and carried out a CT scan, treatment, endoscopy, and biopsy.

They provided detailed explanations using printed notes, text, and photos. They explained the next steps and the costs, which was very reassuring. I was also relieved that they immediately reported to my regular vet.

Despite the high cost, there were many dogs and cats in the waiting room.

It made me very happy to see how much they are loved.

Thank you very much.
It was certainly expensive, but it was our last hope after other hospitals turned us down. Thank you so much for your help.

I regret going to the doctor.

The hatred will never go away.

My cat is an 11-year-old female. She visited the oncology department on August 21st.

Last November 10th, she was referred to the urogenital veterinary department by her regular veterinarian. There, she was diagnosed with lymphoma in both kidneys.

The veterinarian who treated her was very clear in their explanation and gave me a trustworthy impression.

Under the veterinarian's guidance, she continued chemotherapy at her regular veterinarian's.

She was doing very well and was in good spirits, but on July 29th, I noticed swelling near the base of her left nose. I immediately took her to my regular veterinarian, who recommended another visit to a specialized medical center due to suspected metastasis.

An appointment was made, and this time it was a visit to the oncology department.

Up until she entered the examination room for testing, she was very energetic (the chemotherapy was working very well) and not in a critical condition at all.

I understand that a consent form for anesthesia is required for the tests.

The tests cannot be performed without consent.

I entrusted my pet to them with complete trust, but a few hours later, I received a call saying,
"His breathing stopped after the anesthesia wore off. We are currently performing CPR, please come to the reception desk immediately."

When I rushed there, I found my child lying there, horribly changed.

"Why did this happen? Give him back!" I cried out, tears streaming down my face.

He was intubated and unconscious, and I was told he was "brain dead."

How did this happen?

Until I asked, I received no detailed explanation, and even that was only,
"It's likely that some tissue or bleeding blocked an organ."

No definitive explanation was given.

I felt no sincerity or respect for life whatsoever.

Due to a blunder during the examination, my precious child has fallen into an irrecoverable state.

I signed the "consent form for anesthesia for the examination," but I did not intend to consent to "blunders during the examination procedure."

If they had properly examined and treated my pet, this wouldn't have happened. I deeply despise the veterinarians who, ignoring their own mistakes, resorted to the word "euthanasia."

My pet remained intubated the entire time, and all I could do was talk to him and stroke him. It's incredibly sad, heartbreaking, and frustrating. I deeply regret having the examination done.

The veterinarian who treated my pet last year was clear in their explanations and trustworthy, but this oncologist was vague in their words, leaving me filled with anxiety and dissatisfaction.

If they advertise "advanced medical care," then I think it's unacceptable that there's such a difference in the level of their veterinarians.

I'm so frustrated.

As someone who entrusts their precious pet to a trusted professional, I wanted more warmth in their words and actions, and above all, clearer explanations.

Ultimately, my precious pet passed away that day.

The only consolation is that his final moments took place at home.

No matter how much I wish or pray, he will never look at me with those sweet eyes again.

My pet's life was tragically taken away despite being taken for an examination.

This time, I requested an examination of the "left nasal base area" as a precaution, and I was told that the condition was "in remission." Now, I deeply regret taking him for the examination at all.

I want the veterinary oncologist who treated him to fully realize the irreparable damage he has caused and to feel responsible.

I am filled with so much regret and grief; I will live with this regret for the rest of my life.

Just before turning 17, I started feeling unwell and was referred to this clinic by my family doctor.

I was a little apprehensive after reading some online reviews, but I'm glad I went.

Blood tests and X-rays helped me determine the cause of my symptoms. Dr. Lee explained everything clearly and thoroughly, including the risks and difficulties associated with an MRI.

The cost was quite high, nearly 60,000 yen for the X-rays and blood tests, but I was very reassured by the satisfactory explanation and diagnosis, and by their reassuring words, "Please feel free to call anytime if you have any concerns."

I'm truly glad I went to see them.
They probably have the technical skills. But the expenses are twice as high as a typical animal hospital, which I think is a bit too expensive.
Are there quotas?

Even though I arrived at my appointment time, I wasn't called for 30 minutes. (I was prepared for this, though.)
The waiting room wasn't very spacious, and people kept accumulating, so I think it's best to go with as few people as possible.

This time, I had a CT scan done on my dog.

They finished earlier than scheduled and called me to let me know.

So I was glad I could pick him up earlier.

The cost was about 210,000 yen, but it was about the same as when I had him examined at another specialist facility, so it might not be particularly expensive or cheap.

Insurance will be billed later, so I paid the full amount out of pocket.

The doctor in charge was rather reserved, so some people might like that, while others might not.

He explained things clearly in response to my questions.

I went by bus, and the transportation was convenient. There weren't many places to kill time, so I went back to Ayase Station once, but it was close, so I didn't feel particularly inconvenienced.
They saved my cat with their incredibly advanced medical system. I can't express my gratitude enough.
the best

I went to an orthopedic surgeon on a referral from my regular vet. I trusted them because they said they were "Japan-only," but I was misdiagnosed. My current veterinarian told me, "It was a misdiagnosis. If you had diagnosed it earlier and had surgery done, the after-effects would have been less severe. It's too late now, but it's a shame," and I can't help but feel helpless. For the next 10 years, my precious family member will be unable to run and will have to live with restricted exercise. If I hadn't encountered a doctor who charged high fees but lacked knowledge, my pet wouldn't have had to suffer.

The doctor is very kind and explains things clearly, carefully considering the treatment plan best suited to each individual dog. The tests included a CT scan, X-rays, endoscopy, and blood tests... and they were expensive. At the consultation, they casually mentioned how much the tests would cost, but it ended up costing about 50,000 yen more than that. However, given their advanced technology, it's understandable. In Tokyo, the only advanced medical center is in Hitotsuya, Adachi Ward, so there were license plates from people who had come from far away. Everyone was there with the sole purpose of saving their beloved dogs. The reviews are also quite high.

On Monday, July 15, 2019, I visited this clinic after receiving a referral letter from my regular veterinary hospital.

My dog ​​was diagnosed with congenital patent ductus arteriosus and underwent catheterization surgery, requiring a hospital stay of just under a week and costing 500,000 yen. Without this surgery, he would have died at 2-3 years old, but now he's as healthy as a normal 7.5-year-old dog. I'm so glad I came here. Thank you very much.

I would like to be completely honest about this visit.

The staff's demeanor was polite and their attitude wasn't bad. However, throughout the entire consultation, I felt like they were pushing unnecessary tests, and my distrust gradually grew. As a result, the more I spoke with them, the stronger my doubts became about whether this hospital's purpose was truly to treat pets or simply to charge exorbitant fees for tests.

I originally visited with trust, but I am extremely disappointed. Despite coming for my cat's dental problems, I didn't have the opportunity to speak directly with a dentist. Furthermore, I was recommended more expensive tests that were largely unrelated to teeth, and the explanation for their necessity wasn't convincing.

I spent both time and money, but I didn't feel that either was used effectively. The issue isn't the money itself, but whether that money was being used for truly necessary treatment.

Overall, this visit was a very disappointing experience.

After undergoing bladder stone surgery at my regular hospital on September 13th of last year, I continued to feel unwell. I repeatedly explained the strange symptoms since October, but they simply said, "We'll wait and see," and then performed blood tests in November and December. My condition still remained unresolved, so I continued to visit the hospital every month, and each time they said it was probably due to aging. In February, blood tests were unconfirmed, but they said a spleen removal would be enough. I asked for a referral to this hospital, and on March 2nd, I was diagnosed with stage 5 malignant lymphoma. He was given one to two months to live... I regret not having been referred to this hospital sooner... Dr. Sato immediately recognized my son's patience. Thank you very much. 🙏 Apparently, the first round of chemotherapy is administered subcutaneously via an intravenous infusion called something called El, but my regular hospital told me that if the second round doesn't enter the bloodstream, they won't be able to administer it. If outpatient chemotherapy is an option, I would choose this hospital!

I was referred by my doctor.
The cost of the test was explained to me, and although it was expensive, I was satisfied because they examined me from various angles.
They also helped me understand the cause of my symptoms and advised me on how to proceed.
When I went to my regular doctor the next day, they had already coordinated with me and we were able to discuss what to do next.
I'm really glad I came to see them because they performed the test and quickly coordinated with my local doctor.

This is how our then 15-year-old toy poodle came to see us.
He had been having trouble eating his food for a while, so we took him to our regular doctor for his annual May checkup, where he was diagnosed with a gallbladder mucous cyst.

Medications were administered for a few days, but he also began to show jaundice, so he was admitted to our regular hospital on May 15th. By chance, a surgeon who only comes once a month was scheduled to come, so surgery was performed a few days later on May 17th.
The surgeon was trusted by our regular doctor, and since surgery was the only way to resolve the problem and it was urgent, we made the decision right away.
However, in the end, the gallbladder could not be removed.
(The bile duct was severely blocked, the pancreatitis was present, and the omentum was severely damaged.)
He continued to receive medication and was temporarily discharged on May 24th.
However, he was readmitted to the hospital on May 26th.
Because his levels remained high, our regular doctor warned us that if he continued like this, we would have no choice but to watch over him until his death.

However, he seemed to be doing well (perhaps thanks to the steroids), so I couldn't give up and started considering getting a second opinion on May 30th. When I mentioned this to my family doctor, he said that a referral-only hospital (secondary hospital) would likely be able to provide different treatments, including surgical treatment, and so he referred me to Jarmec.

Luckily, I was able to make an appointment for June 1st, so I headed there immediately after being discharged that morning. Dr. Hayashi was in charge.
He casually presented a solution to the issues that the part-time surgeon at our family hospital had said were impossible to address, and my mind went blank in a good way. What's more, he even performed the surgery that same day...I feel truly lucky.
The surgery was successful, and now he's 16 years old and his liver values ​​are stable.

If I had asked to have the surgery at a hospital with specialized knowledge when he was admitted to our family hospital, I truly regret that I wouldn't have put him under general anesthesia, had his abdomen cut open twice, and left him feeling lonely and confined alone in a small space for two weeks.
I would like to express my gratitude to Dr. Hayashi, who saved my life, and to the other doctors who looked after me 24 hours a day while I was in the hospital.
Honestly, I think the doctors here are all at a different level.

I've heard that surgery for gallbladder mucous cysts is not uncommon, but even when I searched online I couldn't find many cases like ours, so I decided to post my experience and lessons learned in the hope that someone might find them useful.
My regular vet referred me to this clinic, and I had my dog ​​examined. The veterinarian who treated him was very kind and explained the results in detail.
My cat was seriously ill and received excellent care. The hospital had excellent diagnostic equipment and other facilities, which made me feel very at ease during her hospitalization.

The veterinarian explained everything clearly and thoroughly, and although I was initially anxious about my dog's hospitalization, I was able to entrust him with his treatment with peace of mind. The staff were also wonderful, providing kind and thorough guidance, making this a trustworthy hospital.

Our beloved dog, nearing 12 years old, received treatment for a gallbladder mucocele resulting from biliary sludge. We were referred by our regular veterinarian, and despite it being a holiday weekend, they promptly performed tests and explained the test results and surgical procedure clearly, using illustrations.

Although the doctor was young, we felt confident entrusting the surgery to him. They kept us informed frequently during his hospitalization, and the staff's warm and welcoming demeanor during visits was very comforting.

After the surgery, he was understandably weak, but each visit brought a remarkable improvement in his energy. He seemed to have completely bonded with the doctor and staff, and we were almost sad to see him discharged.

We were initially a little apprehensive because it was a large hospital, but it turned out to be a very warm and welcoming environment for animals.

They offer tests that aren't available at typical local veterinary clinics.

The building is very clean.

The veterinarians are very caring and attentive, so pet owners can trust them.

My dog ​​received excellent care there.

It's a hospital that provides treatment and facilities comparable to those for humans.

Since it's only open until 6 PM, I recommend bringing your pet here immediately if a regular vet can't handle their condition.

First, call ahead and describe your pet's symptoms to confirm if they can see them.

It gets extremely crowded on weekends, and there may be no openings.

My dog ​​was referred by our regular vet and was seen and admitted the day after symptoms appeared.

They have a great ICU, and visits are possible for 20-30 minutes each day if desired.

The reception staff and doctors are all very kind.

There is a parking lot, including a place for motorcycles.

However, be aware that it gets extremely crowded on weekends.
Even with an appointment, the waiting times for the doctor's consultation and for payment are far too long, which is a real problem.

Compared to local doctors, it's more affordable, and the receptionists are very kind and polite! It feels classy! The doctor is also very kind and explains things clearly, and instead of just saying "let's do this" or "let's do that," he doesn't do anything that isn't necessary, and he doesn't seem to be doing it just to make money, but he really talks to me with compassion.

I cannot express enough my gratitude to the doctor and everyone at the hospital 😊
We went to several other hospitals before finally arriving at this one.
Thank you for your thorough explanations and for performing the surgery on Louis's tiny body; he's back to his old healthy self.
Thank you so much. 💐
He's happily taking walks in the hot sun and playing with Leo the Siberian just like before.
I pray for everyone's health and the happiness of all the animals that visit.
And one last time,
Thank you.

At the end of January, we were referred by our regular veterinarian and took our beloved cat for a checkup.

Based on the test results, she was scheduled for chemotherapy, and we went for weekly checkups.

Dr. Ito, who was in charge, was incredibly encouraging with his choice of words, and it gave both our cat and our family the strength to fight on.

Sadly, she crossed the rainbow bridge at the end of June.

We were later delighted to receive flowers as a memorial.

The treatment costs are probably higher than other clinics. However, the presence of specialist doctors provides a sense of security.

There is a parking lot, and a bus stop right in front.

We usually dropped our cat off before noon and picked her up around 2 PM, and there are plenty of things to do around the medical center to pass the time.

We are truly grateful to all the doctors and staff who took such good care of us.
Thank you so much for everything. My child is now healthy.

I developed a hemostatic disorder after knee joint surgery and was urgently admitted to this hospital by the hospital where I had the surgery. Thanks to the treatment provided by the doctor in charge, the communication with my regular hospital, and the coordination, I was able to receive a blood transfusion, which saved my life. I also received genetic blood tests, and the results are yet to be determined. Without this hospital, I wouldn't have survived. I'm still hospitalized at my regular hospital, but I'm truly grateful.

Thank you very much.
The facilities are just like those in a human hospital. The explanations were thorough. What an amazing veterinarian!
Thank you for taking care of my beloved cat who had lymphoma.

We had an 8-year-old Chihuahua and a 3-year-old cat in our family. Around November, the 8-year-old Chihuahua developed pyometra (uterine infection), and blood tests at that time showed abnormal liver function values. We went to a local veterinary hospital, and they said that if the liver function improved, they would also take a small sample of liver for further examination, so we had surgery.

However, the liver function didn't improve, and the cause remained unknown. We were referred here, but initially, we were skeptical and went to another veterinary hospital.

At that time, we were told there might be a problem with the gallbladder—perhaps a gallbladder mucocele. They said it wouldn't be easy and advised us to go to a larger hospital, so the next day we were again referred to this hospital, and appointments were made for us to visit immediately.

We went to the gastroenterology department, and our primary doctor was a female doctor named Dr. Sato. We were completely clueless, but we explained, crying, that we weren't particularly wealthy, that we only had this much money on hand, and whether we could use a credit card.

Then she said, "Let's do the absolutely necessary tests now. The cost won't go above this, is that okay?" She drew pictures to explain each step clearly, describing the tests and surgeries.

There are three patterns of gallbladder problems, and it's impossible to know exactly which one it is without surgery, but there are things that can be done. The cost might seem incredibly high, but since she's only 8 years old and there's a possibility she can live a healthy life in the future, the surgery was scheduled for the next day.

The surgery took longer than expected, and the marks from the magnifying glass were still clearly visible. Even when they must have been exhausted from the emergency surgery, they didn't stop working, drawing clear diagrams to explain things to the owner.

Afterward, she was discharged, and the goal was to either perform a curative surgery or see if she would improve with medication alone. However, she started vomiting repeatedly, so we contacted the hospital and rushed there immediately. We were told that tests would be conducted and she might need to be hospitalized depending on the situation, but during those tests, her condition suddenly worsened. When we rushed back, several doctors were already resuscitating her. She regained consciousness once, but since this wasn't the original treatment, we discussed as a family how to minimize her suffering and let her go.

Even then, they were gentle and supportive, helping us understand why this had happened.

The staff in the hospital ward during the surgery were also very kind and made me feel at ease; it's a very comfortable environment to entrust your precious family member to.

The facilities were excellent, the staff were kind, and the doctor didn't push unnecessary tests or painful procedures, nor did he explain the fees properly.

The staff weren't the type to use patients as test subjects for quick profit. After discharge, they even suggested that since prescriptions at their clinic would be expensive, they could share the prescription details with all their clinics and get them filled there instead. They explained that this would be cheaper if they had the time. They were a group of doctors who faced life and death every day, supporting and helping at all times to ensure our pets could return to their families.

I once asked the doctor why he became a veterinarian. He said it was because a pet he had in the past had died and he felt helpless. He apologized for the commonplace story, but my 8-year-old daughter loves Dr. Sato ♥️ and said, "Please save our pet! We believe in you."

The doctor was off work the day our pet passed away, but I called the next day because I really wanted to express my gratitude. He called me back that evening and first expressed concern for my daughter's emotional well-being and offered to help care for her. Our whole family feels that the doctor saved us.

The doctor spoke to us, apologizing for not being able to save our daughter due to her sudden deterioration and for not being able to fulfill our promise to her. However, we are grateful that she was able to spend time with us as a family until the day before we said goodbye.

Later, a beautiful bouquet of flowers arrived at our home as a farewell gift. Knowing that there is a large hospital nearby that provides unwavering support gives us, our remaining family, and any family members we may have in the future, peace of mind. I always tell my daughter to be kind and compassionate, that she has two hands, and to reach out to those in need. I believe this is only possible because of the hospital's excellent policies.

This is the first time we've seen such well-equipped facilities and excellent doctors, and I believe it will have a significant impact on our daughter's future, as she learned important lessons.

Honestly, there were times when I wondered whether the surgery saved her another month, hastened her death, or if it was worth putting her through such a painful operation for just one more month. But I've come to believe that no child could have been so fortunate to have been cared for by such wonderful doctors.

We are truly filled with gratitude. Dogs and cats are important members of the family, so it's best if nothing happens, but if something does happen and you're in trouble, I recommend visiting this clinic.

Thank you so much!

My cat was hospitalized for a month, from December 12th to January 11th.

Due to the long-term stress of moving, my cat developed a rectal perforation. As a foreigner, there were many technical terms I didn't understand, but the doctor was very kind and explained everything in detail on paper. I don't think my cat would have recovered without the doctor's help. I'm truly grateful.

The cost was a little high, but considering the 24-hour care provided by the nurses, I think it was worth the price.
My elderly Shiba Inu received a full day of examinations and veterinary checkups. Thank you so much. Thanks to you, she can now live out the rest of her life in peace.

Thank you so much for your help!

Chihuahua, 2.5 kg, 13 years and 7 months old (female) …
I received excellent care for my beloved dog during the long weekend due to a sudden illness. …

It was a nerve-wracking place, but...
The staff were all very nice.
It's easily accessible by car, and also a short bus or taxi ride away, so the …

Going first thing in the morning meant we easily found parking, the clinic was clean, and the doctor explained everything thoroughly... I felt completely at ease entrusting my beloved family member to them. …
